cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: Three days of rain on the Spine. The pound is rising faster than the paddles can pass it down. The east flight is already full of boats waiting for water they now have too much of.

left.label: Run all paddles down the east flight
left.outcome: The lower pounds slop over their towpaths. Halfway stays dry.

right.label: Hold the water; let the flight clear
right.outcome: Cellars begin to whisper.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: Sorry. The aqueduct's running a third of what the table says it should for the season. The pound isn't falling a third faster. I've checked. I keep checking.

left.label: Check again, with me
left.outcome: You walk the aqueduct together. It is a trickle. The pound is not.

right.label: Be glad the pound holds
right.outcome: "I am. That's what worries me. Roughly."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. Wind's from the west, hard. The top gate won't hold shut against it without a man on the beam all night. And I've only got two men.

left.label: You stand the beam
left.outcome: A long night. The gate holds. So, barely, do you.

right.label: Requisition a man from the inn
right.outcome: Ilse sends her potboy. He is not pleased. She is less.

cards.speaker: tamm
cards.text: Ice on the pound by morning if this holds. I can rig a boom to keep the gate clear, a day's work and my good timber. Or we chance it.

left.label: Rig the boom
left.outcome: Ice, by morning. The gate clear. Tamm's timber gone.

right.label: Chance it
right.outcome: No ice. Tamm shrugs. "Next time."

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: The water is low, Keeper, and the town is anxious. We would hold the Lamp Vigil at the sill tonight. It costs nothing but a night's passage, and a little belief.

left.label: Close the gate for the Vigil
left.outcome: Lamps on the water. The queue, unexpectedly, joins in.

right.label: Hold it on the bank
right.outcome: "The water hears from the bank as well." She does not believe that.

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: A hot, still week. The pound has a skin of green on it and the gauge has dropped two marks in three days. Boats are starting to touch the sill going in.

left.label: Restrict to light drafts
left.outcome: Heavy barges wait or unload. Nobody grounds.

right.label: Pass everything, carefully
right.outcome: One grounds. Half a day to float her off.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: I've drawn the pound's level against rainfall for a year. Rain makes it rise. But it falls at the same rate whether it rained or not. Something feeds it, and something takes from it. Sorry.

left.label: Keep drawing
left.outcome: "I will. I wasn't going to stop. I just wanted someone to know."

right.label: Show it to Vosk
right.outcome: "Oh. No. Sorry. Not her." She takes the drawing back.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Lightning's struck the chapel weathervane and half the town's on the towpath watching it smoke. Nobody's at the paddles. Three things, and they're all that.

left.label: Let them watch
left.outcome: The vane falls into the pound with a hiss. Cheering.

right.label: Back to the paddles
right.outcome: Grumbling. The vane falls unseen.

cards.speaker: tamm
cards.text: The top gate's lower beam is soft. It'll hold or it won't. If it won't, it'll be in a storm. There's one coming. A week's work, and I'd start today.

left.label: Start today
left.outcome: The gate is out for a week. The storm finds a new beam.

right.label: After the storm
right.outcome: The beam holds. Tamm says nothing, which is how he says 'lucky'.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: A rainbow over the Reed Reach, Keeper. The Hullfolk are out on their decks looking at it. The town says it is a sign. I say it is a gift. What do you say?

left.label: A gift
left.outcome: She is pleased. The town is pleased. It is also a rainbow.

right.label: Rain and sun
right.outcome: "So it is. Both are given."

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: Snowmelt from the Spine. Every stream on the north bank is running brown into the pound. Every stream except one, which runs clear and cold and does not seem to come from the snow.

left.label: Walk up the clear stream
left.outcome: It comes out of the hill below the sluice house, and nowhere else.

right.label: Streams are streams
right.outcome: The pound rises. The boats float. That is the job.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: The west paddle gear's seized with frost. I can free it with a fire under the gear, which is roughly how the Dry Year keeper lost his eyebrows, or wait for noon.

left.label: Light the fire
left.outcome: Gear freed by the second bell. Eyebrows intact. Barely.

right.label: Wait for noon
right.outcome: Six boats wait with you.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Heatstroke. Two hands down and Stroud says it's the third day of this that kills. We can work the paddles at night instead, if the boats will have it.

left.label: Night working
left.outcome: The queue mutters and then sleeps through the passage.

right.label: Work through it
right.outcome: The third man goes down at the fifth bell.

cards.speaker: tamm
cards.text: Storm's brought a whole tree down across the pound below the Reach. Boats can't pass it. I can cut it, two days. Or the Hullfolk can, one day, for a price they haven't said.

left.label: Tamm cuts it
left.outcome: Two days. Good firewood.

right.label: Ask the Hullfolk
right.outcome: One day. The price is the firewood, and a nod.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: The undercroft is damp again. Only damp. It happens when the pound is high, and only then, though the chapel is well above the bank. We tend it. We do not ask why.

left.label: Ask why
left.outcome: "Because it is old, Keeper." She does not meet your eye.

right.label: Send hands to bail
right.outcome: The hands bail. Hale is grateful and does not show them the far corner.

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: Mist on the pound at dawn, and in it, from the north bank, the sound of water running where no stream is marked. By the time the mist lifts the sound has stopped.

left.label: Mark the place
left.outcome: Below the sluice house. You write a bearing in the Ledger.

right.label: Mist plays tricks
right.outcome: The day's boats arrive and the sound is forgotten.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: The reservoir report's late again. It's always late when the pound's low. I've started writing my own. It doesn't agree with theirs. It doesn't agree with the pound either.

left.label: Send yours to the Board
left.outcome: "Oh. All right. Sorry. Yes." She does not sleep that night.

right.label: Keep yours in the drawer
right.outcome: "The drawer. Yes. It's getting full."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Flood debris in the chamber: a hen coop, a door, a dead sheep. The hands want a mark each to go in after it. The sheep, Keeper. It's the sheep.

left.label: A mark each
left.outcome: The sheep is removed with ceremony.

right.label: It's the job
right.outcome: It is done. Slowly. With looks.

cards.speaker: tamm
cards.text: Dry weather's opened the seams on the top gate. She's weeping a hand's width a watch. I can caulk her in the water, badly, or drain the chamber and do it right.

left.label: Drain and do it right
left.outcome: A closed gate for a day. A dry gate for a year.

right.label: Caulk in the water
right.outcome: She weeps less. She still weeps.

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: A week of soft rain and the pound is up two marks for the first time since you came. The gauge, for once, is going the right way. The hands are almost cheerful.

left.label: Bank it: pass fewer boats
left.outcome: The pound keeps its gain. The queue does not thank you.

right.label: Spend it: clear the queue
right.outcome: A record day. The gauge, by evening, is where it was.
